I’ve been asked why I supported this budget package, and the short answer is that it turns good intentions into real opportunities: we prioritized large-scale investments in training because too many people in our community want work that pays a living wage and a pathway to a career, not dead-end jobs, which is why the bill directs $2.8 billion to expand training programs that connect employers and workers, funds 40,000 new apprenticeships so young people and career-changers can earn while they learn, and backs $350 million in wage supports and career services to help people move into higher-paying roles — those are not abstract promises but measurable investments that have helped more than 220,000 workers get placed or upskilled so they can support their families and shop at our local businesses;
